question: In a column or row, which row should the Layers list show first?
context: The UI entry mock (ui-entry-wt.html) lists the Login column in reading order. The app lists the top of the stack first, as Photoshop and Figma do. Mocks are the floor, so a departure needs your answer.

options.label: Top of the stack first, as today
options.summary: Layers keeps listing whatever sits on top first, everywhere. In the Login column the Password field is listed above the Headline, and a Button dropped at the bottom of the column appears at the top of the list.
pros: Matches Photoshop and Figma, which list auto-layout children this way
One rule for every group, free or laid out
cons: The list reads upside down against the screen it describes
Differs from the UI entry mock
options.mitigation: Selecting a row still rings the piece on the canvas, so where it sits is never in doubt.

options.label: Reading order in rows and columns
options.summary: A group laid out as a column lists top to bottom, a row left to right, matching the mock: Login, Headline, Subhead, Email field, Password field, then the Button you drop. Free groups and the canvas keep top of the stack first.
pros: The list reads like the screen
cons: Two orders in one list: a free group and a column read opposite ways
Dragging a row up in a column moves it up on screen, but up in a free group moves it in front
options.mitigation: The two orders only differ inside laid out groups, where front and behind rarely matter.
